overview: The CC Energy & Environment Committee serves as an advisory body focusing on sustainability, climate resilience, and environmental policy in Medford. Its work includes drafting local ordinances for tree protection, promoting building electrification through the Electrify Medford program, and managing community waste reduction initiatives. Meeting since early 2023, the committee has transitioned from setting foundational priorities to tracking the city’s comprehensive Climate Action and Adaptation Plan. By late 2026, the committee was focused on municipal rodenticide restrictions, analyzing greenhouse gas inventories, and overseeing school energy projects.

threads.name: Tree Protection and Ordinances
threads.summary: The committee spent several years developing and revising municipal tree ordinances to protect the public and private tree canopy. Initial discussions focused on reforestation legislation and the need for a certified arborist to support local regulations. The committee formally endorsed draft ordinances for public and private property in early 2024, emphasizing data transparency and mitigation fees for removals. By late 2026, the public tree ordinance received a favorable vote from the City Council Committee of the Whole, while the committee continued to monitor state legislation regarding homeowner tree insurance protections.

threads.name: Electrify Medford and Heat Pump Advocacy
threads.summary: Building and transportation electrification became a core priority in 2023, leading to the development of the 'Electrify Medford' outreach campaign. The program utilizes a grant-funded network of energy coaches to help residents navigate heat pump installations and Mass Save rebates. Regular updates track coach recruitment, community tabling events, and efforts to address resident 'cold anxiety' regarding heat pump technology. Recent work includes coordinating the program with state-level initiatives like the Mass Save Community First Partnership.

threads.name: Waste Management and Zero-Waste Initiatives
threads.summary: The committee manages various waste reduction efforts, ranging from citywide curbside composting to specific initiatives like a survey of restaurant takeout containers to eliminate black plastic. Significant debate occurred in 2026 regarding a proposed transition to bi-weekly trash collection and the implementation of a pay-as-you-throw system. Members have explored diverse strategies including repair cafes, specialty recycling for plastic film, and waste diversion at large-scale community festivals. Recent efforts include researching model ordinances for single-use plastics and zero-waste programming.

threads.name: Rodent Control and Rodenticide Restrictions
threads.summary: Sparked by the poisoning deaths of local bald eagles, the committee has consistently advocated for alternatives to anticoagulant rodenticides. Early work focused on promoting carbon dioxide treatments and rodent birth control as part of integrated pest management. The committee has since engaged with state-level advocacy groups and researchers to understand the ecological dangers of these toxins on natural predators. By late 2026, the committee was actively researching municipal levers for enacting bans and exploring model lighting ordinances to complement pest management goals.

threads.name: Climate Action Plan Tracking
threads.summary: The committee serves as a primary monitor for the city's Climate Action and Adaptation Plan, which encompasses approximately 150 individual action points. This work involves reviewing greenhouse gas emissions inventories, which show a downward trend in building energy emissions through 2024. Members use a tracking spreadsheet to perform gap analyses on strategies ranging from zoning recodification to grid reliability. In late 2026, the committee began data collection for the formal five-year review of the plan.

threads.name: Municipal Energy and Building Projects
threads.summary: The committee oversees environmental standards for municipal infrastructure, including school HVAC upgrades and the electrification of the city fleet. Key projects include the installation of solar arrays at the McGlynn School and the library, and advocating for LEED Platinum certification for the new high school. The committee also reviews the city's electricity aggregation contracts, which have increasingly prioritized renewable energy content. Recent updates involve the deployment of electric vehicle charging stations and monitoring the sustainability design of new fire stations.

threads.name: Harvest Your Energy Festival
threads.summary: The annual Harvest Your Energy Festival is the committee's flagship community outreach event, focusing on recycling, energy education, and sustainability. The event includes electronics recycling, on-site paper shredding, wind turbine tours, and an electric vehicle showcase. Each year the committee coordinates logistics such as vendor recruitment, volunteer shifts, and shuttle services. The festival typically processes over 1,000 pounds of materials and dozens of appliances for recycling annually.

periods.narrative: The committee established its foundational priorities, including tree canopy preservation and rodenticide alternatives, while initiating regional climate resilience webinars.
This period focused on the launch of the Electrify Medford coaching program, the formal endorsement of tree ordinances, and in-depth educational presentations on chemicals like PFAS.
The committee transitioned to high-level tracking of the Climate Action Plan and debated significant municipal waste policy changes including bi-weekly trash collection.
